lead_decisions: Budget is per turn, not per page: before a tool result would push the next continuation body past a safety margin under 65,536B, return a structured CONTEXT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED result with bytes left and next_query for a NEW turn. Never let a model-followed next_query lock the conversation.

Pre-send over-cap rejection (encode_body refuses before any byte is written to the provider socket) must not leave the conversation as outcome_unknown: nothing was transmitted, so end the turn in a recoverable state and release the reservation, proven by a test that asserts zero provider writes. If ledger semantics make this unsafe, stop and report evidence instead of inventing a path.
General search_project_context lists (shots, actions, plans) get the same explicit truncation count + next_query treatment.
Pending scene proposals beyond 10 per scene: no new model fetch path (the model never approves; humans review in Scene Studio). Keep the count + omitted flag and say so in the result.
Pending preference candidates with different values: cap open candidates (default 10, same as the scene pending limit) with a structured refusal; reversible default.
locked_fields re-check stays out of scope (needs a new lock store) and remains a user-decision defect.
OpenAI strict tool schemas: move minLength/maxLength into the description via a wire transform like anthropic_wire_schema; do not send unsupported keywords.
UI: index.html:418 and scene-studio.js:154 notices are removed/condensed and their test expectations updated in the same task (user approved structural fixes for all 52 confirmed findings).
.lt-cost-facts is only for real cost/transmission facts; non-cost scope notes move to muted text or disclosure; real warnings use the warning token.
Stray __pycache__ .pyc writes: not deleted (deletion needs explicit user permission); recorded as a finding; workers must make every subprocess they spawn inherit -B / PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
